entities.summary: The central teacher of the Buddhist tradition-complex, remembered as Siddhattha Gotama; traditional accounts and scholarly reconstructions date him differently.
Mauryan emperor (r. ca. 268-232 BCE) whose edicts document patronage of Buddhist institutions.
South Asian philosopher associated with the Madhyamaka treatises; his dates remain disputed between the 2nd and 3rd centuries CE.
Chinese pilgrim whose 5th-century account records monasteries and practices from Chang'an to Sri Lanka.
Chinese pilgrim and translator whose 7th-century record and translations shaped East Asian Buddhism.
Translator active at Chang'an whose teams rendered Madhyamaka and Lotus texts into Chinese.
Silla monk noted for commentaries and for accounts of practice outside formal monastic rank.
Japanese regent remembered in chronicles as a patron of Buddhism in the Asuka period.
Pilgrimage town in Bihar associated with the teacher's awakening; excavated temple remains date from the Mauryan period onward.
Deer-park site near Varanasi remembered as the setting of the first teaching; Ashokan-period remains survive.
Excavated monastic-university site in Bihar, active from the 5th century CE.
Oasis-town corridor site; the Mogao caves preserve Buddhist painting and manuscripts from 366 CE onward.
Tarim-basin oasis kingdom on the northern route; a translation center before Kumarajiva's move east.
Han-Tang capital and translation center where Faxian, Xuanzang, and Kumarajiva worked.
Cliff-temple complex south of Luoyang begun under Northern Wei patronage after 493 CE.
Ancient Sri Lankan capital and seat of the Mahavihara lineage.
Hill site traditionally linked with Mahinda's arrival in Sri Lanka.
Temple site in Lhasa associated with the imperial-period introduction of Buddhism to Tibet.
Mountain venerated across Buddhist, Bon, Hindu, and Jain accounts; pilgrimage circuits are recorded from the imperial period onward.

activity.displayExpression: Traditionally venerated across Buddhist, Bon, Hindu, and Jain accounts

entities.summary: Silla capital and temple-building center from the 6th century CE.
Excavated Silla temple site in Gyeongju, founded in 569 CE.
Japanese capital region of the Nara period and early temple-building center.
Basin district west of Nara holding the Horyu-ji temple area.
Monastic university drawing students from across Asia; Xuanzang studied here.
Anuradhapura fraternity remembered as the custodian of the Pali commentarial tradition.

activity.displayExpression: Traditionally founded in the 3rd century BCE

Temple in Ikaruga holding early Japanese Buddhist sculpture and architecture.
Silla temple complex in Gyeongju developed from the 8th century.
Lhasa temple associated with the imperial-period establishment of Buddhism.
Pali discourse remembered as the first teaching; transmitted in the Samyutta Nikaya.
Sanskrit sutra family on the single vehicle; widely translated in Central Asia and China.
Short wisdom text circulating in Sanskrit and Chinese versions.
Pali chronicle composed at the Mahavihara, carrying Sri Lankan traditional history.
Faxian's record of monasteries between Chang'an and Sri Lanka.
Xuanzang's record of Nalanda and the western regions on his return.
Verses attributed to Nagarjuna and read as the Madhyamaka root text.
Japanese court chronicle whose Buddhism passages underlie competing introduction dates.
The Mahavihara lineage preserved in Sri Lanka and identified with Theravada transmission.
A family of movements oriented to the bodhisattva ideal, visible in texts and inscriptions of the early centuries CE.
Esoteric transmissions documented from the 7th-8th centuries, with earlier ritual antecedents.
A meditation-oriented lineage whose early history mixes documented teachers with retrospective genealogy.
Gathering remembered as the first communal recitation after the teacher's passing.

Founding of the Hwangnyong temple in the Silla capital.

Traditional founding of the Mahavihara fraternity at Anuradhapura.
